_meta.purpose: Store identity and behaviour. The second of the two files a cloned store edits - this one plus design-tokens.json. See PROJECT_PLAN.md Section 1.1.
notes: This is NOT .env. .env holds secrets and per-environment values (database URL, Stripe keys) and is git-ignored. This file holds store identity, is committed, and is identical in development and production for the same store. A clone changes this file; it does not change .env for the same reasons.
Read by both the backend (app/store.py) and the web app. One file, two readers - so currency and tax cannot disagree between what checkout charges and what the storefront displays.

features.variants_enabled = false hides the variant picker in the UI. It does NOT mean products can exist without variants: inventory and cart_items both hang off product_variants, so a variant-less product is unsellable. A single-variant product with empty attributes is how a store with no meaningful variant dimensions is modelled - see seed.py's Canvas Tote Bag.
Feature flags are declared here before the UI that reads them exists (Phase 3 tasks 5-6). Until then they are inert on the web side, though the backend already honours the catalog and money values.

store.tagline is the one line of store voice the storefront shows in two places (home hero and footer). It lives here rather than in a component because a clone selling candles must not have to edit page.tsx to change it.

home.featured is merchandising, and it is optional. Set featured.category to a category slug to put a band above the catalogue grid; leave it empty and the band does not render at all, which is the correct state for a clone that has not decided what to lead with. Every string in it is store voice, which is why none of it lives in the component - the same argument as store.tagline, one level up in ambition.

home.featured.image is a deliberate second choice rather than the featured category's first product photograph. The lead shot is a merchandising decision: it may be a lifestyle frame that is not a product image at all, and deriving it would silently hand that decision to whichever product sorts first alphabetically.
